messages.subject: Re: Can I use the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for analyzing dichotomous items?
parts:
Dear Yves,

Here is code:

mod.sem <- "
school_forest =~ school_forest1 + school_forest2 + school_forest3
optimism =~ optimism03 + optimism07 + optimism10
happiness_at_school =~ happiness_at_school03 + happiness_at_school04 + happiness_at_school09 + happiness_at_school10 + happiness_at_school16 + happiness_at_school17 + happiness_at_school23
eXtroversion =~ eXtroversion04 + eXtroversion05 + eXtroversion07 + eXtroversion09 + eXtroversion10 + eXtroversion14 + eXtroversion15 + eXtroversion17

happiness_at_school ~ school_forest + optimism + eXtroversion 
school_forest  ~ optimism + eXtroversion 
"
lavaan.fit2 <- sem(mod.sem, data=rawdata_dich, estimator="DWLS") # It works!
summary(lavaan.fit2, fit.measures=T, standardize=T)
survey.design2 <- svydesign(ids=~school_name, prob=~1, data=rawdata_dich)

survey.fit1 <- lavaan.survey(lavaan.fit=lavaan.fit2, survey.design=survey.design2, estimator="MLM") # It works!
summary(survey.fit1, fit.measures=T, standardize=T) 
 
survey.fit2 <- lavaan.survey(lavaan.fit=lavaan.fit2, survey.design=survey.design2, estimator="DWLS") # fail for works.
summary(survey.fit2, fit.measures=T, standardize=T)

I was failed to estimate a result with DWLS estimator in lavaan.survey(), not lavaan() and not MLM with lavaan.survey().
I have 100 samples per group, across 19 groups. (n=1900)

lf who wants a raw data, I'll upload on here.

--
Seongho Bae.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Can I use the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for analyzing dichotomous items?
parts: The syntax looks fine. But you have dichotomous items, so
> lavaan.fit2 <- sem(mod.sem, data=rawdata_dich, estimator="DWLS") #

did you forget to declare the items as 'ordered'? As in

lavaan.fit2 <- sem(mod.sem, data=rawdata_dich, estimator="DWLS", ordered
= c("school_forest1", "school_forest2", ....))

or are they already declared as 'ordered' in the data.frame? You can
check this by running

varTable(rawdata_dich)

> survey.design2 <- svydesign(ids=~school_name, prob=~1,
> data=rawdata_dich)

The svydesign() function can NOT handle categorical (endogenous) variables.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Can I use the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for analyzing dichotomous items?
parts:
On 09/18/2014 09:36 AM, Seongho Bae wrote:
> How can I use the MML estimator?
> I tried to find a manuscript, but I can't.

the MML estimator is still experimental.

> Which command is correct?

> or lavaan.fit2 <- sem(mod.sem, data=rawdata_dich, estimator="MML",
> ordered=names(rawdata_dich))

This one is correct: whatever estimator you are using, you always need
to specify which variables are 'ordered'.

But if you have several factors, MML will take forever. The mirt package
is much more efficient (and uses c++ code).

Yves.
